summary: Property-setter that updates the Name=Value pair in a TStrings backing store. When the named entry already exists the existing line is rewritten; when absent a new line is appended. Setting a value to empty string deletes the entry entirely (this is a Delphi-VCL convention that does not map cleanly to .NET Dictionary or Java Map — explicit Open Question to the SME).

inputs.name: AName
inputs.semantic: Name portion of the Name=Value pair. Case-insensitive matching follows the underlying TStrings.CaseSensitive flag.

inputs.name: AValue
inputs.semantic: New value. Empty string triggers deletion semantics (see EC-1).

invariants.claim: After the setter returns, FList.Values[AName] equals AValue when AValue is non-empty.
When AValue is empty string, the AName entry is removed from FList (matches Delphi VCL TStringList.Values setter contract).
FList.Count strictly decreases by 1 when AValue is empty AND AName previously existed; strictly increases by 1 when AValue is non-empty AND AName did not previously exist; unchanged otherwise.

property_accessors.semantic: Indexed-property setter; the published Value property delegates here.

side_effects.description: Mutates FList — the backing TStrings — via either Insert, Delete, or in-place line rewrite. Subscribers to FList.OnChange observe the mutation.

event_handler_contracts.contract: TStringList fires OnChange after every mutation (Insert / Delete / line rewrite). Translating to .NET: an INotifyPropertyChanged 'Item[]' event or an ObservableCollection.CollectionChanged. Translating to Java: a Listener on a custom ObservableNameValueStore.

edge_cases.description: AValue is empty string. Delphi VCL convention: deletes the AName entry. Callers occasionally rely on this for 'clear without erase'.
edge_cases.behavior: Setter deletes the line. INV-3 applies.

edge_cases.description: AName contains '=' character. TStrings.Values setter parses on the first '=' so an AName containing '=' silently truncates at the first occurrence.
edge_cases.behavior: Resulting Name=Value pair will have the truncated AName; the rest becomes part of the value. SME confirms this is the desired (non-) behaviour or files an Open Question.

open_questions.question: Should the .NET / Java translation preserve the 'empty value deletes' convention? Most .NET / Java caller idioms expect an empty value to be stored verbatim. Recommend filing as a target-language idiom break and surfacing in the scaffold archetype as a TODO.
Is the AName-contains-'=' truncation behaviour load-bearing for any caller in the corpus? If not, the .NET / Java translation can throw ArgumentException for cleanliness.
